question: Identify the L1_model associated with each model (specified by name and version) that occurs most frequently for each status ('strong' or 'soft'), along with the number of times it occurs. A model has a 'strong' status if, for any of its steps, the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models is less than the 'Stack' model's test score. It has a 'soft' status if the maximum test score among non-'Stack' models equals the 'Stack' model's test score. Count how many times each L1_model is associated with a 'strong' or 'soft' status across all models, and determine which L1_model has the highest occurrence for each status.
sql:
-- Final comprehensive answer
WITH scores AS (
    SELECT name, version, step,
           MAX(CASE WHEN model = 'Stack' THEN test_score END) as stack_test_score,
           MAX(CASE WHEN model != 'Stack' THEN test_score END) as max_nonstack_test_score
    FROM model_score
    GROUP BY name, version, step
),
step_status AS (
    SELECT name, version, step,
           CASE 
               WHEN max_nonstack_test_score < stack_test_score THEN 'strong'
               WHEN max_nonstack_test_score = stack_test_score THEN 'soft'
           END as step_status
    FROM scores
    WHERE stack_test_score IS NOT NULL
),
model_status AS (
    SELECT name, version,
           MAX(CASE WHEN step_status = 'strong' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as is_strong,
           MAX(CASE WHEN step_status = 'soft' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as is_soft
    FROM step_status
    GROUP BY name, version
),
model_l1 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT name, version, L1_model
    FROM model
),
status_counts AS (
    SELECT 'strong' as status, ml.L1_model, COUNT(*) as occurrence_count
    FROM model_status ms
    JOIN model_l1 ml ON ms.name = ml.name AND ms.version = ml.version
    WHERE ms.is_strong = 1
    GROUP BY ml.L1_model
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'soft' as status, ml.L1_model, COUNT(*) as occurrence_count
    FROM model_status ms
    JOIN model_l1 ml ON ms.name = ml.name AND ms.version = ml.version
    WHERE ms.is_soft = 1
    GROUP BY ml.L1_model
)
SELECT status, L1_model, occurrence_count
FROM status_counts
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC) = 1
ORDER BY status
